sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: public health outreach manager: begin evidence gathering before service launch

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the outreach calendar and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The service map review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can schedule a clinic information session when the referral route and interpreter coverage are confirmed.
Are new outreach sessions usually hard to arrange?
No, not when people know where follow-up care will come from.
Someone new shadowed me in the health hub this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the campaign periods into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The neighbourhood wellbeing idea proposes weekend drop-ins, but it identifies neither referral partners nor the languages needed by the largest resident groups.
What is unsafe about promising the programme now?
We could invite people to disclose needs without a clear route to appropriate support.
A recent vaccination pop-up worked because the clinic reserved appointments before we advertised it.
What did that avoid?
Sending people to seek a service that had no capacity for them.
I archived last cycle's notes on the service map and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The hub has funds for listening sessions and can print multilingual information once languages are identified.
Can that run the full service?
No, it can map needs and prepare a responsible first offer.
A vendor call about the outreach calendar ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the health hub checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the campaign periods.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the service map records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The local clinics have agreed to review the listening-session findings and reserve referral slots if the need and language plan are confirmed.
What can you commit to today?
Listening sessions and service mapping, with any drop-ins dependent on that joint review.
I sketched next week's plan for the campaign periods before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the outreach calendar updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The campaign team must submit its autumn calendar in five weeks.
Does that require advertising weekend drop-ins?
No, it can list the listening sessions and a later service decision.
A communications agency says a broad launch message would show the hub is responsive.
Does that create referral capacity?
No, responsiveness is not the same as a route for care.
I closed the week by updating the health hub handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I announce recurring weekend wellbeing drop-ins for the neighbourhood?
